text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello, it's you. I said you looked like my husband, I hope you don't mind.
A: Hello. I'm Martin. I'll take that as a compliment, I think.
B: You should, he's very sensible. I'm Claire. I'm in Otley, near Leeds.
A: Oh, our son lives in Leeds. Headingley, I think it's called.
B: Headingley, yes, lots of students and cricket. We're just up the road from there. Where are you?
A: Lewes, in East Sussex. I noticed the postcard from Lisbon in your photo, actually. I'm learning Portuguese at the moment, rather slowly.
B: No! I love Lisbon. We went a few years ago, all those hills and the little yellow trams, and I just kept ordering custard tarts and pretending it was lunch. Why Portuguese?
A: Well, er, I walked part of the Camino through Portugal and felt a bit foolish only having Italian. So there's an app, and a conversation group on a Wednesday night where I mostly apologise.
B: Ha, that's me with my Korean. I'm learning it on an app, on and off, mostly off. What do you do, Martin? I've been told by Callum you know your books.
A: Have you? That's kind of him. I'm a structural engineer, mostly old bridges and masonry. People send for us when a Victorian arch has cracked and they'd like to know whether it's going to fall down.
B: And is it?
A: Usually not. They're more forgiving than people think. What about you?
B: Speech and language therapist, NHS, with little ones. So I'm sort of on the floor with toy buses all day trying to get a shy four-year-old to say anything at all. And I love it. The paperwork, less so.
A: I'm the same with reports. The interesting part is out on site. The writing up is where it all goes wrong.
B: Yes! Do you know what I mean, you've done the actual thing, why do I have to write it all down as well. Sorry. Is that a piano behind you, in your photo?
A: My wife Helen's. She teaches music. I don't play, I just get told when I'm humming flat.
B: Oh, I sing alto in a choir in Leeds, and I'm terrible at learning my parts. We've got a concert soon and there's one bit I just cannot get, I come in a bar early every single time.
A: Helen would say count, and then count again.
B: Everyone says that! I'm sure she's right. Erm, I saw your sketch of a bridge, too. Did you do that?
A: I did, yes. That's the one at Barcombe, near us. I draw them partly for work and partly for the pleasure of it.
B: That's lovely. I do lino prints, the heron and the hare on my board are mine, so the kitchen table's always covered in ink.
A: I thought they were rather good, actually. I wondered whether you'd bought them.
B: Oh, stop, you'll make me blush. Do you cook? Mark does the Sunday roast, but I do tea in the week, whatever comes in the veg box.
A: I do most of our dinners. I tried a Sri Lankan curry last week from a borrowed book. It was nearly right.
B: Nearly right is my whole cooking career, love.
